_about: James Adam (1860-1907), Cambridge Platonist, editor of the Republic. Raw IA OCR: The Religious Teachers of Greece, Gifford lectures delivered in Aberdeen in 1904-06, edited with a memoir by his wife Adela Marion Adam (Edinburgh: T. & T. Clark; printed for the University of Aberdeen, 1908). His commentaries, taken 2026-10-23 under Adam's ruling on Greek-facing editions: The Republic of Plato, edited with critical notes, commentary and appendices (Cambridge, 2 vols., 1902) and the Protagoras (with A. M. Adam, 1893); also The Vitality of Platonism (1911) and The Nuptial Number of Plato (1891). US public domain. No uids minted.

james-adam-republic-1902-v1: The Republic of Plato, edited with critical notes, commentary and appendices, vol. I: Books I-V (Cambridge: University Press, 1902); Greek text with English commentary, kept per Adam's 2026-10-23 ruling

james-adam-nuptial-number-1891: The Nuptial Number of Plato: its solution and significance (London: C. J. Clay, 1891)
